chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Muawiya ibn A'yan, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Ibn Abi Layla asks me to bear witness that this house belonged to so-and-so who died and left it as inheritance, and that he has no heir other than the one for whom we have testified.' He said: 'Bear witness to what is upon your knowledge.' I said: 'Ibn Abi Layla makes us swear with an oath of certainty (Ghamus).' He said: 'Swear, for it is merely upon your knowledge.'

key_terms.بِغَمُوس: With an oath of certainty (a specific type of oath used in legal contexts)

ai.seo_question: What is the basis for valid testimony according to the Imams: personal knowledge or absolute certainty?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the principle of *al-shahada bi ma huwa 'ala 'ilmika* (testify according to what you know), distinguishing between the witness's subjective certainty and objective truth. It addresses the practical legal context of swearing by *Ghamus* (a specific oath of certainty) to validate property inheritance claims, affirming that such oaths are permissible as they reflect the witness's personal knowledge rather than implying infallibility. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the reliability of individual testimony in civil matters when supported by appropriate oaths.
